title: PagerDuty brief cards with latency-slice and rollback commands
creator: Ravi Desai
description: Problem: On-call responders currently receive verbose PagerDuty alerts that lack a concise, actionable summary tailored to latency spikes. During incidents engineers spend the first 5-15 minutes hunting for the right traces, relevant dashboards, and safe rollback/mitigation steps. Goal: Build a compact "brief card" attached to PagerDuty incidents that bundles a prioritized latency slice summary, one-click jump-to-trace links (sampled), related error-rate histogram, and contextual rollback or mitigation commands derived from runbooks. The brief card should reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for latency-driven incidents while preserving lightweight payloads for PagerDuty and Slack attachments.
design_notes: High-level approach: 1) Use existing trace sampling pipeline to synthesize a single concise trace summary (span waterfall + top 3 suspicious spans) for the top latency percentile in the last 5 minutes. 2) Query metrics pipeline for p99/p95 trends and an error-rate histogram for the service. 3) Attach an excerpt of the canonical runbook (first 3 steps + quick rollback commands) based on service tags and incident taxonomy. 4) Deliver as a compact JSON card to PagerDuty and as an expanded Slack message with action buttons. Implementation details: - New lambda-style 'incident-brief' microservice that receives an alert webhook, performs fast lookups (traces via trace-index, metrics via metrics-query cache), composes the card using our attachment spec, and calls PagerDuty/Slack APIs. - Add a lightweight authorization step reading incident tags to include safe rollback commands (only include commands for services with 'manual-rollback-allowed' flag). - Respect rate limits and ensure attachment size < 8KB for PagerDuty. - Fallback: if tracing data unavailable, surface top N logs from logstore + top error messages.
acceptance_criteria: When a latency alert fires for a service in the 'web-prod' namespace, a PagerDuty incident includes a brief card with: one-line hypothesis, p95/p99 delta, link to sampled trace, and first-3-runbook-steps.
Brief card attachment payload size remains below PagerDuty attachment limits (< 8KB) in 99% of alerts; if exceeded, card truncates to key pointers and adds 'view full playbook' link.
Slack channel expansion shows the full sampled trace waterfall and provides an actionable 'Initiate rollback' button that executes only after SSO confirmation (via existing ops-runbook service).
No sensitive credentials or unapproved commands are embedded in attachments; rollback commands are templated and validated by ops-runbook allowlist.

Automated tests cover card generation logic for: trace present, trace missing (fall back to logs), and metric-only alerts. Load test ensures microservice can handle 1000 alerts/min with median processing latency < 200ms.
Runbook excerpt mapping covers 95% of services in production catalog; unmapped services fall back to generic mitigation steps and flag a follow-up PM/Docs ticket.
implementation_steps: Create incident-brief microservice skeleton and API contract
Wire trace-index fast query for top-latency span extraction (5m window)
Add metrics-query cache lookup for p95/p99 deltas
Implement runbook excerpter and ops-runbook allowlist integration
Compose PagerDuty/Slack attachment payloads and add size safeguards
Add feature flag gate and gradual rollout to prod namespaces
Write unit/integration tests and run 1k alerts/min load test
Ship behind feature flag; monitor MTTA/MTTM and card rejection rates
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Attachment could leak internal commands. Mitigation: enforce ops-runbook allowlist and run security review before rollout.
Risk: Trace queries add latency to alert pipeline. Mitigation: use cached trace-index and fall back to logs; add circuit-breaker and time budget of 150ms.
Risk: PagerDuty or Slack rate limits throttle attachments. Mitigation: batch similar incidents and send pointer-only card when limits hit; monitor 429 metrics.
Risk: Incorrect runbook mapping causes wrong mitigation steps. Mitigation: require manual approval for runbook additions and staged rollout to low-risk namespaces.
test_plan: Unit tests for trace extraction and stringification (edge cases: absent spans, empty tags)
Integration test: send synthetic latency alert, validate PagerDuty payload and Slack expanded message via staging integrations
Canary rollout: enable for 'canary-web' namespace for 48 hours and measure MTTA/MTTM and false-action rate
Chaos test: simulate trace-index downtime and validate fallback to logs and graceful degrade of card payload
rollout_notes: Feature will be behind 'incident-brief-cards' feature flag. Start with canary namespaces (canary-web, canary-batch) for 48h, then expand to 25% of production namespaces by service tag. Monitor metrics: incident_card_success_rate, card_size_p95, pd_429_rate, mtta, mttm.
